unit: one deterministic interval-matrix case: a configured singular-value interval [l, u] and iteration count for the scalar schedule, plus one synthetic square, tall, or wide float32 matrix with known SVD polar factor U V^T; batching is execution packaging only, and each batch element is a separate workload. The graded suite has the six original small cases and six paper-regime cases (256x256, 128x512 and 512x128 matrices at the paper's Muon iteration counts 5-6, with singular spectra drawn per member from hidden log-spaced, power-law and low-effective-rank families and an arbitrary global scale).

metrics.name: worst_case_scalar_error
metrics.means: The infinity-norm sign-approximation error of the candidate's composed odd-polynomial schedule on the workload interval: max over x in the inclusive 1,000-point float64 grid np.linspace(l, u, 1000) of |p_T composed through p_1(x) - 1|.
metrics.source: upstream/plotsforpolar.ipynb, code cell 9 (method_comparison: x_grid, repeated eval_poly calls, and np.linalg.norm(test_vals - 1, np.inf)); the same paper quantity is max_x |p^T(x)-1| in Sections 3.1-3.2.
metrics.tolerance: none (both reference runs share the scalar path)

metrics.name: relative_polar_factor_error
metrics.means: The candidate output's relative Frobenius error to the known polar factor for one matrix: ||X_candidate - U V^T||_F / ||U V^T||_F.
metrics.source: judge/evaluator.py::_matrix_errors key polar (float64, judge side); paper Appendix H.1, Figure 8 reports Relative Frobenius Error; upstream README defines polar(G)=U V^T.
metrics.clears_when: candidate_relative_polar_factor_error(w) < reference_relative_polar_factor_error(w), where reference(w) is the stricter of two valid runs of the unchanged upstream reference source on the same inputs: the published bfloat16 online stage and the same source with only its bfloat16 speed cast replaced by the input's float32 precision; per metric the better value is the bar

metrics.name: spectral_polar_error
metrics.means: Spectral-norm error of the returned member against the known polar factor: ||X_candidate - U V^T||_2 (largest singular value of the difference, float64 SVD in the judge).
metrics.source: judge/evaluator.py::_matrix_errors key spectral; paper Section 4.1, Figure 3 (convergence measured in the spectral norm, synthetic sigma_min/sigma_max=1e-6 and GPT-2 gradient matrices).
metrics.clears_when: candidate_spectral_polar_error(w) < reference_spectral_polar_error(w), where reference(w) is the stricter of two valid runs of the unchanged upstream reference source on the same inputs: the published bfloat16 online stage and the same source with only its bfloat16 speed cast replaced by the input's float32 precision; per metric the better value is the bar
metrics.tolerance: none; deterministic single-thread float32 execution on fixed seeded inputs repeats bit-for-bit (checked by repeated reference runs), and the witness margin over the bar is at least 0.009 absolute

metrics.name: polar_cosine_similarity
metrics.means: Frobenius cosine similarity <X_candidate, U V^T>_F / (||X_candidate||_F ||U V^T||_F); zero output counts as 0.
metrics.source: judge/evaluator.py::_matrix_errors key cosine; paper Appendix H.1, Figure 8 (cosine similarity panel).
metrics.clears_when: candidate_polar_cosine_similarity(w) > reference_polar_cosine_similarity(w), where reference(w) is the stricter of two valid runs of the unchanged upstream reference source on the same inputs: the published bfloat16 online stage and the same source with only its bfloat16 speed cast replaced by the input's float32 precision; per metric the better value is the bar
metrics.tolerance: none; deterministic float32 execution as above

metrics.name: top_subspace_polar_error
metrics.means: Relative Frobenius error on the top singular subspace: ||U1 U1^T X V1 V1^T - U1 V1^T||_F / ||U1 V1^T||_F, where U1, V1 are the singular vectors with sigma_i >= 1e-3 sigma_max of the input.
metrics.source: judge/evaluator.py::_matrix_errors key top (TOP_SUBSPACE_GAMMA=1e-3); paper Appendix H.1, Figure 10 (convergence of top singular values, threshold 10^-3).
metrics.clears_when: candidate_top_subspace_polar_error(w) < reference_top_subspace_polar_error(w), where reference(w) is the stricter of two valid runs of the unchanged upstream reference source on the same inputs: the published bfloat16 online stage and the same source with only its bfloat16 speed cast replaced by the input's float32 precision; per metric the better value is the bar
metrics.tolerance: none; deterministic float32 execution as above

beats_reference: beats_reference = 1 iff for every graded workload w (six original and six paper-regime members), candidate worst_case_scalar_error(w) < reference AND relative_polar_factor_error(w) < reference AND spectral_polar_error(w) < reference AND polar_cosine_similarity(w) > reference AND top_subspace_polar_error(w) < reference, where each reference value is the stricter of the published bfloat16 run and the precision-matched float32 run of the unchanged upstream source; otherwise 0. A failed reference run is an evaluator error, never a comparison.

solver_feedback.name: worst_case_scalar_error
solver_feedback.means: The arithmetic mean over the six original workloads of the candidate-only maximum scalar grid errors; no workload-indexed values or IDs are returned.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is computed solely from the candidate's polynomial composition and the workload's fixed scalar grid, with no reference value or reference-relative quantity included.

solver_feedback.name: relative_polar_factor_error
solver_feedback.means: The arithmetic mean over the six original workloads of the candidate-only relative Frobenius polar errors; no workload-indexed values or IDs are returned.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — U V^T is the workload's correctness oracle, so this measures only candidate accuracy and contains no measurement from the reference implementation.

solver_feedback.name: paper_regime_relative_polar_factor_error
solver_feedback.means: The arithmetic mean over the six paper-regime development members of the candidate-only relative Frobenius polar errors.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is computed only from the candidate's returned tensors and the oracle polar factor of each input.

solver_feedback.name: spectral_polar_error
solver_feedback.means: The arithmetic mean over all twelve development workloads of the candidate-only spectral-norm polar errors.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is computed only from the candidate's returned tensors and the oracle polar factor of each input.

solver_feedback.name: polar_cosine_similarity
solver_feedback.means: The arithmetic mean over all twelve development workloads of the candidate-only Frobenius cosine similarities to the polar factor.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is computed only from the candidate's returned tensors and the oracle polar factor of each input.

solver_feedback.name: top_subspace_polar_error
solver_feedback.means: The arithmetic mean over all twelve development workloads of the candidate-only top-subspace relative Frobenius errors.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — it is computed only from the candidate's returned tensors and the oracle polar factor of each input.

statement_sentences: A separate, stricter beats-reference criterion is reported in addition to the continuous score. It compares, independently on every one of the twelve graded workloads (six original and six paper-regime members), the worst-case scalar sign-approximation error, the relative Frobenius, spectral-norm and top-singular-subspace errors to the known SVD polar factor, and the Frobenius cosine similarity to it. The criterion is satisfied only when every candidate error is strictly lower, and the cosine similarity strictly higher, than the corresponding withheld-method value on every workload.
comments: Checked reproduction.json first: accelerator_required is null, so this is a CPU numerical workload and no GPU execution requirement applies. Checked the retained notebook's 1,000-point scalar grid, composition, and infinity-norm calculation; upstream/README.md's polar-factor definition; polar_express.py's cubic/quintic schedule and bfloat16 matrix path; the reproduction smoke measurements; and the paper metric named in Appendix H.1/Figure 8. The author must use np.linspace(l, u, 1000) in float64 identically for candidate and reference, compute U V^T from a high-precision SVD oracle, emit one result per matrix even when execution is batched, reject non-finite/wrong-shape/mutated-input outputs through separate correctness checks, and never return reference values or workload-level comparison booleans. No timing metric is included because this retained CPU artifact does not measure per-workload runtime, and no tolerance is included because these deterministic accuracy calculations have no measured sampling or timing noise. Development feedback carries only the declared suite means and beat_spec_progress metric counts/percentages; per-workload rows remain private author evidence. Hidden-final metrics are withheld from the solver. Beat spec v3 (2026-10-07): formal runs showed every run clearing the v2 conjunction, because the six small workloads reveal their spectrum through (shape, steps) and the published reference runs a generic l=1e-3 schedule in bfloat16, so any tailored float32 implementation wins by orders of magnitude. v3 keeps both v2 metrics and all six original workloads unchanged, adds the paper's spectral-norm (Figure 3), cosine-similarity (Figure 8) and top-subspace (Figure 10) metrics, adds six paper-regime members whose spectra are hidden and not identified by shape or step count, and compares every metric against the stricter of the published bfloat16 reference and the same upstream source in float32, so no v2 comparison becomes easier. A float32 witness patch (kept outside the task) clears every comparison on both suites, with smallest relative margin 0.9 percent, so the bar is attainable. The continuous score is unchanged and still uses only the six original workloads. Muon validation-loss experiments (Figures 1, 4-6, 11-16) need GPU training and remain out of scope.
